title: Clarinet
summary: A published 1981 Buffet Crampon Prestige bore and tone-hole lattice, blown at the published mezzo-forte mouth pressure with a lumped reed of published mass, stiffness and damping, observed at the physical baffled outlet receiver. Of the 15 fingerings rendered so far, the all-holes-closed D3 and the register-hole note Bb4 speak a clean harmonic series at their pitch; Eb3 (lowest hole open) and A4 (register hole only) speak but carry a line near 1.1 kHz that is stronger than their fundamental; every fingering with two or more lower tone holes open falls into a parasitic regime between 0.8 and 2.6 kHz instead of its fundamental. The same failure occurs for the published reed at its own published pressure. Graded by the P2 tool against the UIowa clarinet recordings: D3 sits inside the real-recording spread on 8 of 15 measures, Eb3 on 12 of 15 (its real-vs-real ruler is very wide, so that is weak evidence), A4 on 3 of 15; Bb4 is refused because its onset is a step that the 1.5 ms alignment rule cannot match to the recording. All of them are much brighter than the recordings, have no breath noise floor, and carry a start-up transient from the bore's priming wave. Diagnostic renders (not landed) that changed only the reed damping ratio did not find the cause: the published 0.0765 and the in-mouth model value 0.2 (q_r 0.4 of Silva, Kergomard, Vergez and Gilbert 2008, arXiv 0810.2870) do not make F3 or G3 speak, 0.3 does, and at 1.0, which is critical damping and not a cited value, F3 to D4 speak while D5 and A5 still do not. Diagnostic renders (not landed) of F3, Ab3, C4, D4, Gb4, D5 and A5 at damping ratio 0.2 changed one more property at a time and found no cited value that separates speaking from parasitic: the committed 3.1 kHz reed, the reed resonances 1883, 2368 and 3687 Hz (Gaillard, Koehl and Gazengel 2024, Acta Acustica 8, 63, Table A7, reed plus lip) and 1500 Hz (just under the 1530 to 1890 Hz of a wet reed on a mouthpiece, Table A6) and a 1.04 cm3 reed equivalent volume (the UNSW clarinet impedance page) leave all seven parasitic. Values outside every cited range do separate them, each only for some notes: a reed resonance of 500 Hz (about 40 times the committed reed mass) lets F3 to D4 speak, 750 Hz lets C4 to Gb4 speak, 1000 Hz lets Gb4 and D5 speak, all flat by up to 55 cents, and A5 never speaks; 4 cm3 of extra input volume lets F3 and Ab3 speak about 110 and 125 cents flat. The cause is open. The specimen is a population proxy for the UIowa R13, not the same instrument.
physics_present: fs-duct transfer-matrix air column built from the published Taillard and Sanchez 2016 bore station table, split at every chimney and never decimated, with the Vandoren M30 exit cone
every tone hole as a side branch (published position, minimal diameter and chimney height) with a flanged open mouth; the Moers and Kergomard 2011 normal-set chart decides which are open
flanged radiation load at the bell and the physical baffled outlet receiver (32 rings x 128 angles, 4.8 kHz band) for the radiated pressure, not the listener_m proxy

lumped single reed with mass, stiffness and damping, from the published Chatziioannou and van Walstijn 2009 set (mass per area, effective area, stiffness per area, damping rate), so the reed has a resonance near 2.5 to 3 kHz; the closing pressure per note follows a declared lip-force rule
mezzo-forte mouth pressure interpolated from Fuks and Sundberg 1996 (two professionals on a Buffet Crampon Prestige), applied after a rest and held
physics_missing: fingerings with two or more lower tone holes open do not speak: the oscillator leaves the fundamental for a bore resonance between 0.8 and 2.6 kHz, and the extra lines of the Eb3 and A4 renders (1085 and 1135 Hz) lie on passive impedance maxima found by an independent plane-wave check, so the line is a real resonance of the modelled bore that the reed regenerates. Reed damping is a lever but not the cause: with the other inputs unchanged F3 and G3 speak at damping ratio 0.3 and 1.0 and not at 0.0765, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20 or (F3) 0.25; at 0.3 F5 also speaks while Ab3, C4, D4, Gb4, D5 and A5 do not; at 1.0 Ab3, C4, D4 and Gb4 speak and D5 and A5 do not. Not yet separated: how several open holes combine in the bore (the fs-duct |Z_in| of every chart fingering agrees with an independent plane-wave check to about 2.3 dB, so the bore model is not the defect; both share the flanged-chimney idealisation), the reed closure, the reed resonance and mass loading in the mouth (a mass-controlled reed at 0.8 to 2.6 kHz suppresses the parasitic line but needs a resonance below every cited value, and no single value serves all notes), hole geometry without undercuts, and the equivalent-cylinder mouthpiece

too bright and too clean: the reed closes against the lay with one very hard contact constant and no lay curvature, so it shuts abruptly and the high partials stay strong; there is no breath or turbulence noise, and the bore's 5 Pa priming wave leaves a start-up transient before the attack

the reed set is a published model parameter set, not a measurement of the Vandoren reed and B40 or James Canter mouthpieces the players used; the effective area S_r is a corrected misprint (printed 7.61e5 m2, read as 7.61e-5 m2) and the damping unit is read as a rate; lip force is a rule, not a measurement; the damping of a reed held by a lip is UNKNOWN (route: artificial-mouth reed and lip impedance tables), and neither the cited reed+lip damping factors (0.03 to 0.24) and resonances (1883 to 3687 Hz) of Gaillard, Koehl and Gazengel 2024, Table A7, nor the in-mouth model value 0.2, make the open-hole fingerings speak
the mouthpiece chamber, baffle, throat and lay are unknown; the cavity is an equivalent cylinder matched to the published internal volume and length
open tone holes do not radiate in the observer (only the bell does), and undercuts, pad geometry and key rise are unknown
dry room-temperature air everywhere: the warm humid breath field is not applied
no wall vibration, no player airway, lips or tongue, no vibrato; the lumped reed has one mode and no reed continuum
the specimen is not the UIowa Buffet R13 and no same-specimen passive comparison exists yet; fingerings outside the normal set have no chart
